title: Why Starlink is faster to respond than old satellite internet
description: The difference is altitude. Closer satellites mean far less delay for each signal.

scenes.say: Old satellite internet felt slow, even when the speed looked fine. The culprit wasn't bandwidth. It was distance.

Traditional satellites sit in geostationary orbit, about thirty-five thousand, seven hundred kilometers above the equator. Starlink's main shell flies around five hundred fifty kilometers up. Typical round trips differ hugely.
Why four legs? Your request goes up and down, then the reply goes up and down again. Even light alone takes about half a second on the high route.

steps: Dish sends request to a satellite
Reply makes the same trip back
scenes.say: In practice, your dish sends the request up, a ground station joins the internet, and the reply returns the same way.
The catch is that low satellites move fast, so you need many, handing you off. Follow for more satellite explainers.
